reference_traces.rationale: Reviewer support for the innovative network-of-networks formulation is retained; final paper evidence P:S-369d5eb1497871dd1a71 defines its arbitrary-shape representation.

The reviewer’s concern about explanatory power remains as a qualified scope limit because final paper evidence P:S-c658fbb5aa80c836089b explicitly states that the simple model does not capture the many mechanisms of brain development.

The reviewer’s positive assessment of an analytically tractable physical-network model is supported by final paper evidence P:S-64213af38d534ea6f70d, which reports agreement between analytical predictions and simulations.

The reviewer’s observation that physical structure constrains dynamics is supported by final paper evidence P:S-841b9270a6218198b298, which derives the volume-normalized physical Laplacian and its coarse-grained interpretation.
The reviewer’s support for degree-volume correlations across physical networks is retained; final paper evidence P:S-352d83b3dfcf80c30340 reports the corresponding pattern in four additional systems.

The reviewer’s request to distinguish the proposed mechanism from known brain-growth processes remains partially open; final paper evidence P:S-c658fbb5aa80c836089b limits the model rather than establishing a mechanistic mapping.
The reviewer’s sensitivity concern is retained as a scope condition. Final paper evidence P:S-134313395e1c9ace9e1c explicitly requires isotropic growth and gives directed growth as a counterexample.

The reviewer’s data-coverage concern remains partially open because final paper evidence P:S-d7c8b5d6df5ea74da162 states that Hemibrain is incomplete and presents an expectation, rather than a full-connectome sensitivity result.

The reviewer asked for conditions under which a real developmental process can be mapped to the model. Final paper evidence P:S-c658fbb5aa80c836089b supports retaining this residual question because it disclaims modeling the many developmental mechanisms.
Audit-only resolved presentation issue: final paper evidence P:S-59fe18fd74b15a179217 explicitly labels the continuous-time treatment as an approximation.
Audit-only resolved evidence-expansion issue: final paper evidence P:S-352d83b3dfcf80c30340 reports analysis of four additional real systems.

limiting_points.suggested_action: Frame the contribution as a general physical-network framework and avoid interpreting its minimal growth mechanism as an explanation of brain development.
limiting_points.text: The methodological contribution is not a mechanistic account of brain development: the paper explicitly states that its simple growth model does not capture the many processes shaping the brain.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Preserve the distinction between the arbitrary-shape network-of-networks representation and sphere-tube physical-network models.
supporting_points.text: The network-of-networks formulation provides an explicitly shape-aware representation of physical nodes and links, extending beyond localized-node and tube-link descriptions.

questions.suggested_action: Specify empirically grounded conditions under which developmental mechanisms can be mapped to the model without attributing similar macro-level patterns to the same micro-mechanism.
questions.text: Which known neural growth mechanisms can satisfy the framework’s assumptions, and which cannot?

strengths.suggested_action: Maintain the direct correspondence between analytical predictions and simulation tests.
strengths.text: The work gives a tractable growth model with explicit predictions for volume evolution, degree-volume proportionality, and degree-distribution scaling that are tested numerically.

strengths.suggested_action: Retain the volume-normalized Laplacian derivation and the correlation-shuffling comparison as the central dynamical evidence.
strengths.text: The volume-normalized physical Laplacian makes clear why combinatorial connectivity alone can miss dynamical effects of heterogeneous node volume and degree-volume correlation.

strengths.suggested_action: Keep the cross-system analyses clearly separated from causal claims about a shared generative process.
strengths.text: The empirical scope extends beyond the fruit-fly connectome to four additional physical systems, each exhibiting positive degree-volume correlation and a suppressed Laplacian spectral tail.

summary.text: The paper introduces a network-of-networks representation for extended physical nodes, develops a minimal growth model linking volume exclusion to degree-volume correlations, and derives a volume-normalized Laplacian to study their dynamical consequences. Simulations and analyses of the fruit-fly connectome plus four additional physical systems support the recurrence of the reported structural and spectral patterns, while the biological interpretation remains deliberately limited to a general framework rather than a detailed developmental mechanism.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Clarify the boundary between a general mechanism for degree-volume correlation and a causal model of neural development, including how omitted growth mechanisms could alter the conclusions.
weaknesses.text: The model’s explanatory scope for the brain remains limited: it does not represent the diverse mechanisms of brain development, and the paper leaves branched growth, guided interactions, and substrate expansion for future work.

weaknesses.suggested_action: State the isotropy/intersection condition prominently wherever the degree and Laplacian conclusions are generalized beyond LERWs.
weaknesses.text: Generality across node-growth processes is conditional on isotropy: strongly directed trajectories can avoid intersection and yield disconnected chains rather than the reported power-law behavior.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Quantify the sensitivity of key spectral and early-spreader results to incomplete hemispheric and whole-brain coverage when suitable data are available.
weaknesses.text: The connectome analysis uses an incomplete Hemibrain dataset; the expected robustness to full-brain coverage is stated but is not directly tested in the final paper.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: The final paper explicitly identifies the continuous-time step as an approximation.
The final paper adds analyses of four additional real systems.
